newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Competition Bureau rejects gas claims.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Competition Bureau rejects gas claims.

text.p: Canada's Competition Bureau said on Tuesday that its investigation into the gasoline industry found no evidence to support allegations of price fixing, anti-competitive behavior or misleading advertising.
"No evidence of any competition offence was found," Konrad von Finckenstein, director of investigation and research for the bureau, said in a statement.
The bureau initiated four gasoline inquiries last spring and summer after allegations about several major gasoline companies.
There was no evidence to support the claim that the major gasoline companies had engaged in a national price-fixing conspiracy, the bureau said.
The bureau said it also dismissed a second claim that Ultramar Canada Inc's Value Plus marketing campaign was predatory pricing aimed at eliminating competition.
A price war in Quebec and the eastern provinces last summer was "an indication of healthy competition for market share," the bureau said.

The investigation also found no evidence to support an allegation that Ultramar and other regional and national petroleum companies were squeezing the profit margins of independent petroleum markets with the intention of forcing the independents out of business.
"The evidence indicated that declining margins being earned by large and small Canadian petroleum companies are the result of competition and the restructuring in the industry," the bureau said.

The bureau also looked into claims that national and regional petroleum companies were selling gas at prices below cost. It concluded that the pricing was a result of a price war in Quebec and not an attempt to eliminate or discipline gasoline retailers.
The bureau also found that Ultramar did not make any misleading statements in its advertising campaign.
